observations.title: Session summary: pago_prestamos
observations.content:
## Goal
Fix the balance display issue where the UI showed stale balances because `updateLoan` fails silently in production (Appwrite document permissions).

## Discoveries
- Appwrite document-level `update` permission needs to be explicitly granted for client SDK to update documents, even if collection-level permissions are set.
- The `updateLoan` call from client SDK fails silently (no error thrown, but DB not updated).
- UI can be made resilient by computing effective balance from `payments[0].balance_after_payment` instead of relying on `loan.current_balance` from DB.
- TanStack Query `useQueries` intercepts query keys with the same prefix; simpler approach is a single flat query for all payments + `useMemo` map.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Added `getAllPaymentsForUser` service function to loanService
- ✅ Added `useAllPaymentsSummary` hook that fetches all payments for current user
- ✅ Created `getEffectiveBalance()` utility function
- ✅ Updated `LoanDetailPage` to compute `effectiveBalance` from `payments[0].balance_after_payment`
- ✅ Updated `LoanListPage` to use a `useMemo` map of loanId→balance from all payments
- ✅ Updated `LoanCard` to accept explicit `balance` prop
- ✅ Added try/catch to `useUpdatePayment` mutation (same pattern as create)
- ✅ Invalidated `payments-summary` query key on payment mutations so list refreshes

## Next Steps
- Deploy to Easypanel with `git push` and verify both list and detail pages show correct balances
- Add `user_id` index on payments collection in Appwrite for efficient `getAllPaymentsForUser` queries

## Relevant Files
- src/features/loans/services/loanService.ts — added getAllPaymentsForUser()
- src/features/loans/hooks/usePayments.ts — added getEffectiveBalance(), useAllPaymentsSummary(), try/catch in updatePayment, payments-summary invalidation
- src/features/loans/pages/LoanListPage.tsx — uses effective balance via useMemo map of loanId→balance

observations.title: Fixed PDF sync 500 error - Blob upload instead of base64 server action
observations.content:
**What**: Replaced base64 server action upload with binary Blob + FormData via dedicated API route for PDF sync in reports, quotes, and invoices.

**Why**: PDFs with photos produced base64 strings exceeding the 20MB `serverActions.bodySizeLimit`, causing 500 errors on `POST /reportes/{id}/imprimir` and the misleading "Error al extraer datos" catch-all message.

**Where**: 
- `src/app/api/upload-pdf/route.ts` (new) — accepts FormData, uploads to Appwrite Storage via REST
- `src/app/(print)/reportes/[id]/imprimir/PrintButton.tsx` — Blob + FormData + /api/upload-pdf
- `src/app/(print)/cotizaciones/[id]/imprimir/PrintButtons.tsx` — same fix
- `src/app/(print)/facturas/[id]/imprimir/PrintButtons.tsx` — same fix
- `next.config.ts` — increased `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` from 20mb to 100mb

**Learned**: Next.js server actions POST to the page URL with a configurable body size limit. Base64 inflates binary by ~33%, making this worse. Using `pdf.output('blob')` + `FormData` to a dedicated API route avoids both the size limit and the inflation overhead. The `uploadDocumentPdf` server action is now unused (can be cleaned up later). The API route uses direct REST to Appwrite per appwrite-rest-compliance rules.

observations.title: Session summary: grupo-ecotech
observations.content:
## Goal
Diagnosticar y resolver el error de sincronización de PDFs (ERP-686) en la generación de informes de servicio técnico con fotos grandes.

## Instructions
- Trabajar en español cuando el usuario lo solicite
- Preferir soluciones server-side robustas sobre workarounds client-side
- Siempre hacer build (`npm run build`) para verificar cambios

## Discoveries
- La API REST de Appwrite Storage espera `fileId` como nombre del campo multipart, NO `documentId`. El SDK de node-appwrite abstrae esto pero REST directo no.
- `html2pdf.js` convierte DOM→canvas→PDF en cliente — frágil con fotos grandes (OOM) y el payload excede Server Actions.
- La página de imprimir usa `@media print` con `position: fixed` en header/footer — Puppeteer puede generar PDF directamente con `page.pdf()` respetando estas reglas.
- Puppeteer v25 se auto-descarga Chromium durante npm install (no necesita postinstall explícito).
- `Blob` en Node.js 20 necesita `Buffer.from(pdfBuffer)` por un mismatch de tipos entre `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` y `BlobPart`.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Corregido `documentId` → `fileId` en endpoint `/api/upload-pdf` (bug inmediato)
- ✅ Instalado `puppeteer` para generación server-side de PDFs
- ✅ Creado endpoint `/api/generate-pdf` que lanza Puppeteer, navega a la página imprimir en localhost, genera PDF con `page.pdf()`, lo sube a Appwrite vía REST, y retorna view URL
- ✅ Reescrito `PrintButton.tsx` — reemplazado html2pdf (CDN) por fetch a `/api/generate-pdf`
- ✅ Reescrito `triggerSilentPdfSync` (`pdf-sync.ts`) — reemplazado iframe+postMessage por fetch directo al API
- ✅ Build exitoso sin errores
- ✅ Removida dependencia de html2pdf.js (cargado desde CDN) del PrintButton de reportes

## Next Steps
- Hacer deploy a EasyPanel para probar que Puppeteer/Chromium funciona en el servidor
- Si Chromium no funciona en EasyPanel (sin root), migrar a `puppeteer-core` + `chrome-aws-lambda` o alternativa
- Actualizar PrintButtons de cotizaciones y facturas para que también usen `/api/generate-pdf` (opcional, el auto-sync ya pasa por el API)
- Agregar variables de entorno para los bucket IDs (actualmente hardcodeados en el API)

## Relevant Files
- `src/app/api/generate-pdf/route.ts` — Nuevo: endpoint Puppeteer para generar PDF server-side
- `src/app/api/upload-pdf/route.ts` — Corregido: `documentId` → `fileId`
- `src/app/(print)/reportes/[id]/imprimir/PrintButton.tsx` — Modificado: html2pdf → API

observations.title: Puppeteer + Nixpacks build: Chrome download and system library fixes
observations.content:
**What**: Fix múltiple para que Puppeteer funcione en producción con Nixpacks/Easypanel: build pasó de 500 "Param fileId not optional" a generación de PDF server-side funcional.

**Why**: Se necesitaba generación de PDF server-side (Puppeteer) porque html2pdf.js fallaba en producción (loading infinito). /api/upload-pdf tenía error 500 por campo FormData mal nombrado.

**Where**: 
- src/app/api/generate-pdf/route.ts — endpoint Puppeteer
- nixpacks.toml — config build Nixpacks
- .nixpacks/packages → eliminado
- src/app/(main)/dashboard/page.tsx — version bump

**Learned**:
- El error "Param fileId is not optional" en /api/upload-pdf: el campo en FormData se llamaba `documentId` pero Appwrite Storage espera `fileId`. El fix fue en el frontend (renombrar campo).
- Para Puppeteer en Nixpacks:
  1. NO usar `executablePath` con `/usr/bin/chromium` — la ruta del chromium del sistema no es confiable en Nixpacks.
  2. Solución correcta: dejar que Puppeteer descargue su propio Chrome (NO poner PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD).
  3. Solo se necesita `unzip` en aptPkgs para extraer Chrome.
  4. Se necesitan TODAS las librerías del sistema (libnss3, libatk1.0-0, libatk-bridge2.0-0, libcups2, libgbm1, libasound2t64, libpangocairo-1.0-0, libxss1, libgtk-3-0, libxshmfence1, libglu1, libglib2.0-0) instaladas via `[phases.setup].aptPkgs` para que Chrome pueda ejecutarse.
  5. `.npmrc` con `puppeteer_skip_download=true` NO funciona porque no es config de npm, es variable de entorno.
  6. `[phases.install].variables` en nixpacks.toml funciona para build-time ENV.
  7. `[phases.setup].aptPkgs` en nixpacks.toml REEMPLAZA los paquetes auto-detectados por Nixpacks, no los suma. Hay que listar TODO explícitamente.
  8. Nixpacks v1.41: los paquetes en aptPkgs se instalan via apt-get, el `chromium` que auto-detectaba antes venía de Nix + auto-detection, no de apt explícito.
- Regla de versioning: cada feature/bugfix obligatorio incrementar versión en UI (Dashboard).

observations.title: Fixed Router Cache causing stale data — staleTimes + missing revalidatePath
observations.content:
**What**: Eliminated the 30-second Router Cache staleness and added 4 missing revalidatePath() calls  
**Why**: User noticed some UI updates required F5 to appear. Root cause was Next.js 15 Router Cache (30s TTL for dynamic pages) + missing revalidatePath() in 4 server actions  
**Where**:  
- next.config.ts — added staleTimes: { dynamic: 0, static: 0 }  
- src/actions/field-reports-chat.ts — revalidatePath('/reportes') in getOrCreateDraftReport and addChatMessage

**Learned**: staleTimes is an experimental feature in Next.js 15.5. Chat components (ChatWindow, TechnicianProfileView) don't need router.refresh() because they use optimistic local state — calling it would disrupt the server component tree during active chat. router.refresh() is needed in list/table views (QuotesView, FieldReportList) where data must reflect server state after mutation.

**Why**: User reported email subject still showed old format (#394E155B), WhatsApp showed #REP-REP-14158, and image uploads showed #REP-4E155B  
**Where**:  
- src/actions/emails.ts:341 — reportRef now uses report.customNumber  
- src/services/skills/intent-router.js:565 — shortReportId uses customNumber, template #${shortReportId} (no duplicate REP-)

observations.title: Invoices show quote customNumber instead of $id slice
observations.content:
**What**: Store quoteCustomNumber on invoice at creation time and display it instead of quoteId.slice(-6)  
**Why**: Converting a quote to an invoice showed #1C8A6F (old $id slice) instead of COT-3895 (customNumber)  
**Where**:  
- src/actions/quotes.ts:346 — added quoteCustomNumber to invoice payload in convertQuoteToInvoice  
- src/actions/field-reports.ts:710 — added quoteCustomNumber to invoice payload in generateInvoiceFromReport  
- src/features/invoices/components/InvoicesView.tsx:30 — added quoteCustomNumber to Invoice type  
- src/features/invoices/components/InvoicesView.tsx:844 — displays inv.quoteCustomNumber || fallback  
**Learned**: Storing the quote's customNumber on the invoice at creation time avoids needing extra DB fetches at display time. Fallback to $id.slice for existing invoices that don't have quoteCustomNumber.

observations.title: Fixed invoice creation error — fetch quote customNumber at query time
observations.content:
**What**: Removed quoteCustomNumber from invoice createDocument payload (Appwrite rejects unknown attributes) and instead batch-fetch quote customNumbers in getInvoices  
**Why**: Previous approach tried to store quoteCustomNumber on invoice at creation time, but Appwrite rejects attributes not defined in the collection schema  
**Where**:  
- src/actions/quotes.ts:347 — removed quoteCustomNumber from createDocument  
- src/actions/field-reports.ts:710 — removed quoteCustomNumber from createDocument  
- src/actions/invoices.ts:16-44 — getInvoices now batch-fetches quotes via listDocuments and attaches quoteCustomNumber to each invoice  
**Learned**: Appwrite validates document attributes against collection schema. Unknown fields cause runtime errors. Fetching related data at query time (batch via listDocuments) avoids schema changes and handles existing documents naturally.

observations.title: Architecture decision: normalized batch fetch vs denormalized for quote references on invoices
observations.content:
**What**: Chose normalized batch fetch (query-time join) over denormalized field for displaying quote.customNumber on invoice list  
**Why**: Appwrite rejects attributes not defined in collection schema. Two approaches were considered:  
  1. Normalized (chosen) — getInvoices batch-fetches all referenced quotes via listDocuments and attaches quoteCustomNumber to each invoice at query time  
  2. Denormalized — store quoteCustomNumber on the invoice document at creation time (requires creating the attribute in Appwrite Console + migration script for existing invoices)  
**Where**: src/actions/invoices.ts — getInvoices() batch fetch logic  
**Learned**: For current scale (dozens of invoices, few concurrent users), normalized is correct: Single Source of Truth, no data duplication, no schema migration. If scale grows to hundreds of invoices and high request volume, migrate to denormalized — it's a trivial migration since quoteId already exists on every invoice. Recommendation: keep normalized for now, defer denormalization until there's actual performance evidence it's needed. This decision applies to any cross-collection reference pattern in this project.

observations.title: Implementado drag-and-drop en vistas Semana y Mes de Agenda
observations.content:
**What**: El DnD solo estaba en la vista Agenda (lista) por el DndContext anidado en renderAgendaList. Se movió DndContext al wrapper superior que cubre todas las vistas y se envolvieron los chips de Semana y Mes con DraggableCard/DroppableDay para permitir arrastrar citas entre días. Se agregó PointerSensor con activationConstraint distance:5px para que clicks en botones internos no disparen drag accidental.

**Why**: User reportó "drag and drop no funciona". Diagnóstico: el viewMode default es 'month', y en month/week/day no existía DndContext (chips eran <button> planos via renderApptChip). Solo Agenda lo tenía.

**Where**: src/features/appointments/components/AgendaView.tsx
- imports: agregado PointerSensor, useSensor, useSensors de @dnd-kit/core
- handleDragStart/handleDragEnd y rescheduleAppointment(apptId, targetDate) siguen igual (solo cambia fecha, no hora)
- DraggableCard/DroppableDay generalizados con props style/className/onClick
- renderWeekView: cada columna de día -> DroppableDay, cada chip -> DraggableCard con position absolute
- renderMonthView: celdas null siguen como <div> plano, las con fecha -> DroppableDay con onClick a vista día; los <button> de cita -> DraggableCard
- renderAgendaList: se quitó DndContext anidado y DragOverlay interno (se movieron afuera)
- return JSX: bloque de las 5 vistas ahora envuelto en <DndContext sensors={sensors}...> con <DragOverlay> al final

**Learned**:
- Vista Día NO recibe DnD: solo muestra un día y rescheduleAppointment solo cambia fecha; para hora haría falta otra action.
- @dnd-kit/core no soporta DndContext anizado limpio; mejor tener uno solo en el wrapper.
- Sin activationConstraint, los clicks en botones internos (Edit/Delete/etc del AppointmentCard) pueden disparar drag; distance:5px lo evita.
- /agenda arroja 500 sin sesión (getCurrentProfile en el server component). No se puede testear Playwright sin creds.
- tsc --noEmit pasa limpio; npm run lint requiere setup interactivo (next lint deprecated).

observations.content:
## Exploration: Landing Page de Alta Conversion para TEACHPADAH

### Current State
El proyecto tiene un index.html (647 lineas) standalone en la raiz, una landing page comercial funcional para TechPadah enfocada en servicios de automatizacion con IA. Es autosuficiente y no depende de la app Next.js.

Elementos existentes: tema oscuro con accent naranja (#F7941D) y azul (#3B3B98), Three.js via CDN para particulas 3D, canvas starfield vanilla JS, loader con barra de progreso, navbar con transformacion a pill en scroll, scroll progress bar, hero con chat demo animado, specs con count-up, services en cards glass-morphism, how-it-works con tabs interactivas, CTA con boton WhatsApp, floating WhatsApp button (wa.me/50765153531), footer, fade-up animations.

Que NO tiene: widget de chat web en la pagina, captura de leads funcional, conexion entre landing page y app Next.js, web chat embed.

Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript 5.7, Tailwind CSS 3.4, shadcn/ui (New York), Appwrite v16. La app Next.js es stubs (placeholder home page, auth y dashboard vacios). Solo src/lib/appwrite/ tiene configuracion real.

### Affected Areas
- index.html — landing page existente (standalone approach)
- src/app/page.tsx — home page de Next.js (Next.js approach)
- src/app/layout.tsx — metadata y root layout
- tailwind.config.ts — necesita extension de tema
- src/features/ — nueva feature landing
- src/lib/appwrite/ — integracion lead capture
- package.json — posibles dependencias (three, framer-motion)

### Approaches

1. Enhance index.html directamente — Agregar widget de chat web, formulario de captura y mejoras de conversion.
   - Pros: Cero friccion, funcional hoy, sin build step, deploy inmediato
   - Cons: Sin TypeScript, sin reuso de componentes, no integrado con app
   - Effort: Low

2. Rebuild como Next.js landing page — Reescribir landing como src/app/page.tsx con React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui.
   - Pros: TypeScript, componentes, Appwrite SDK, chat widget React, mantenible
   - Cons: Alto esfuerzo (647 lineas a reescribir), animaciones complejas en React, riesgo de regresion visual
   - Effort: High

3. Hybrid: Chat widget embed + form en index.html — Mantener index.html, agregar chat embed y endpoint serverless en Next.js.
   - Pros: Esfuerzo balanceado, funcionalidad real de chat, backend en Next.js
   - Cons: Dos codebases divergentes, chat externo puede tener costo
   - Effort: Medium

### Recommendation
Enfoque 2 (Rebuild Next.js), faseado:
- Fase 1: Migrar estructura visual y copy (hero, specs, services, CTA) a React + Tailwind
- Fase 2: Agregar widget de chat web como componente React
- Fase 3: Three.js via @react-three/fiber, scroll animations con framer-motion, lead capture con Appwrite

### Risks
- Regresion visual en animaciones canvas/Three.js al migrar a React (mitigacion: @react-three/fiber + framer-motion)
- Nuevas dependencias aumentan bundle (mitigacion: dynamic imports con next/dynamic)
- No existe backend de chat web (solo WhatsApp link). Requiere decision de implementacion
- Coexistencia temporal de dos landing pages puede confundir SEO
- Skill website-3d asume video frame-sequence; no hay video disponible. Enfoque actual usa chat demo animado, no scroll-driven video

### Ready for Proposal
Yes. El orchestrator debe preguntar: tipo de chat widget preferido, si quiere captura de leads, si prefiere migrar a Next.js o mantener standalone, y cual es el backend de chat

Enfoque exclusivo en conversión vía WhatsApp (sin chat web ni captura de leads).

## Scope

### In Scope
- Reimplementar `index.html` como `src/app/page.tsx` con React 19 + Tailwind CSS 3.4
- Componentes colocalizados en `src/features/landing/` siguiendo arquitectura feature-first
- Animaciones 3D con `@react-three/fiber` (Three.js en React) y scroll animations con `framer-motion`
- Tema oscuro con variables CSS (`--accent: #F7941D`, `--blue: #3B3B98`) replicado en Tailwind config
- CTA principal y botón flotante apuntando a WhatsApp (`wa.me/50765153531`)
- Loader con barra de progreso, navbar pill, scroll progress bar
- Tipografía: Space Grotesk + Archivo vía `next/font/google`

### Out of Scope
- Widget de chat web embebido (decisión: solo WhatsApp)
- Formulario de captura de leads con Appwrite
- Conexión entre landing page y dashboard/app Next.js
- Lógica de negocio o backend (página puramente estática/presentacional)
- Cambios en `src/app/(auth)/` o `src/app/(main)/`

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `landing-page`: Landing page de alta conversión con WhatsApp CTA, animaciones 3D (@react-three/fiber), scroll animations (framer-motion) y diseño profesional dark theme con acentos naranja/azul

### Modified Capabilities
- (ninguna — la landing actual es standalone y no modifica features existentes)

## Approach
Reescritura completa del `index.html` como página Next.js, sección por sección:

1. Crear `src/features/landing/` con componentes por sección (Hero, Specs, Services, HowItWorks, CTA, Footer)
2. Migrar animaciones: canvas starfield → `@react-three/fiber` partículas, Three.js CDN → import ES module
3. Animaciones de entrada con `framer-motion` (fade-up, staggered reveals)
4. Loader inicial como componente React con `useState` + `useEffect`
5. `tailwind.config.ts`: extender tema con colores accent/blue, glass-morphism utilities
6. El `index.html` original se conserva hasta que la versión Next.js esté validada

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `src/app/page.tsx` | Replaced | Home page actual (stub) → landing page completa |
| `src/features/landing/` | New | Componentes de landing: Hero, Specs, Services, HowItWorks, CTA, Footer, Navbar, Loader |
| `src/app/layout.tsx` | Modified | Metadata (title, description, OG) para SEO |
| `tailwind.config.ts` | Modified | Extensión de tema con colores accent/blue, glass utilities |
| `package.json` | Modified | Nuevas dependencias: three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, framer-motion |
| `index.html` | Retained | Coexiste hasta validación completa de versión Next.js |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Regresión visual en animaciones 3D al migrar de CDN a @react-three/fiber | Medium | Comparar side-by-side con screenshots; mantener CDN como fallback |
| Bundle size por three/framer-motion | Low | `next/dynamic` con `ssr: false` para componentes 3D |
| Coexistencia de dos landing pages confunde SEO | Low | Conservar `index.html` solo en branch de feature; eliminar antes de merge |
| Animaciones de scroll complejas difieren del original | Medium | Test visual exhaustivo con Playwright screenshots |

## Rollback Plan
1. Revertir `src/app/page.tsx` al stub original
2. Eliminar `src/features/landing/`  
3. Remover dependencias three/framer-motion de `package.json`
4. Restaurar `tailwind.config.ts` y `layout.tsx` a estado previo
5. `index.html` original permanece intacto durante todo el proceso

## Dependencies
- `three` + `@react-three/fiber` + `@react-three/drei` (partículas 3D)
- `framer-motion` (animaciones de entrada y scroll)
- `next/font/google` (Space Grotesk, Archivo — ya usadas en index.html)

- [ ] Landing page renderiza en `/` con diseño visual indistinguible del `index.html` original
- [ ] Animaciones 3D (partículas) funcionan sin errores de consola
- [ ] Animaciones de scroll (fade-up, stagger) se ejecutan correctamente
- [ ] CTA de WhatsApp abre `wa.me/50765153531` en nueva pestaña
- [ ] Loader con barra de progreso funciona en carga inicial

## Capability: `landing-page`

Landing page de alta conversion para TEACHPADAH, migrada desde `index.html` standalone (647 lineas, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS) a React 19 + Tailwind CSS 3.4 dentro de Next.js App Router. Enfoque exclusivo en conversion via WhatsApp (sin chat web embebido ni captura de leads backend).

- Tailwind extensions: colors (accent #F7941D, accent-glow, blue #3B3B98, bg #0A0A0A), fontFamily (Space Grotesk, Archivo)

## Sections (11 total)

1. **Loader** - Barra de progreso 0→100% en ~3s, fade-out al completar
2. **ScrollProgress** - Barra fixed top, width = scroll%
3. **Navbar** - Fixed, pill transform a scrollY>80, backdrop blur, mobile: links hidden

5. **Specs** - 4 stats con count-up (24/7, 3x, 98%, 0), IntersectionObserver trigger, easing exponencial

7. **HowItWorks** - 2-column: chat demo con tabs (WA/Web/IG) + beneficios; loop infinito por canal
8. **Particles3D** - 3000 particulas Three.js (@react-three/fiber), mouse interaction, overlay texto
9. **Starscape** - Canvas 2D fondo fijo, 180 estrellas con twinkling
10. **CTA** - Urgency badge + WhatsApp button con mensaje predefinido
11. **FloatingWA** - Boton flotante fixed bottom-right, wa.me/50765153531

- Target: _blank, rel: noopener noreferrer

## Animations

- Three.js: 3000 particles, vertexColors (naranja/azul), rotacion + mouse interaction
- Canvas: 180 stars, twinkling alpha, horizontal drift
- framer-motion: fade-up + stagger en services, how-it-works, specs labels
- Custom: count-up hook (1800ms, easeOutExpo), chat demo secuencial (useChatDemo)

- Specs (Interest): 4 metricas de impacto
- Services (Interest+Desire): 3 servicios detallados
- HowItWorks (Desire+Trust): demo + beneficios
- CTA (Action): urgencia + WhatsApp directo

- Tablet (<1024px): 2-col specs, 2-col services
- Mobile (<768px): 1-col services, stacked how-it-works, nav links hidden, spec 2-col

## Performance

- Fonts: next/font/google con display: swap
- Loader: splash screen mientras carga async
- Scroll handlers: passive + requestAnimationFrame
- IntersectionObserver: nativo, sin polling
- Lighthouse target: Mobile >= 70

## SEO

- Static generation (no SSR dinamico)
- Semantic HTML, alt text, anchor links, canonical URL

## Acceptance Criteria

- Visual parity con index.html original
- Loader → fade-out funcional
- Scroll progress + navbar pill funcionales
- Chat demos (hero + how-it-works) animan correctamente

| @react-three/drei | ^9.114.0 | Utility components for R3F | Part of golden stack |
| framer-motion | ^11.0.0 | Scroll and entrance animations | Replaces vanilla IntersectionObserver + CSS transitions |
| @types/three | ^0.170.0 | TypeScript types | Dev dependency for strict mode |

## Loading Strategy

- Particles3D: `next/dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr: false })` with loading fallback
- framer-motion: Static import (SSR-safe)
- Fonts: `next/font/google` with `display: 'swap'` (Space Grotesk 300-700, Archivo 400-900)
- Starfield: Static import inside 'use client' component, positioned fixed behind content

## Tailwind Theme Extension

- colors: accent (#F7941D), accent-glow (rgba variant), blue (#3B3B98), bg (#0A0A0A), surface, muted, border
- fontFamily: grotesk (Space Grotesk), archivo (Archivo)
- Utilities: .glass-card, .glass-hover, .pill-nav, .btn-primary, .btn-secondary

## Component Architecture

Orchestrator: LandingPage → Loader, ScrollProgress, Navbar, Hero (ChatDemo), Specs (useCountUp), Services, HowItWorks (ChatDemo with tabs), Particles3D (dynamic), CTA (WhatsAppButton), Footer, FloatingWA (WhatsAppButton)

## Data Flow

- NEXT_PUBLIC_WHATSAPP_NUMBER → constants.ts (WHATSAPP_URL, WHATSAPP_CTA_URL)
- All content static (no API, no Appwrite, no backend)
- No global state needed
- Single / route, anchor links for section navigation

## Performance Budget

- Particles3D: dynamic import, ssr:false
- Fonts: next/font/google with display:swap
- Animations: GPU-accelerated (opacity + transform)
- Lighthouse Mobile target: >= 70
- JS bundle target: < 200KB gzipped

## Out of Scope

Lead capture form, chat web widget, Appwrite backend, dashboard connection, auth, i18n, blog/pricing, automated tests.

## Risks & Mitigations

- SSR hydration with Three.js → next/dynamic ssr:false
- framer-motion bundle → tree-shaking
- Visual regression → preserve exact timings/easing; Playwright verify phase

- The `appwrite` (web) SDK stores session cookies automatically; server SDK requires manual extraction from cookies

observations.title: Pipeline recorte transparente: Gemini + rembg ISNet
observations.content:
**What**: Pipeline para recortes PNG con transparencia real de imágenes generadas con IA (vector-style cutouts)
**Why**: El usuario pidió las imágenes hero "como vector sin fondo". Gemini NO puede generar transparencia real (devuelve RGB opaco 24bpp aunque se le pida "transparent background").
**Where**: `landing-page/public/images/promo-hero-{robot,phone}-cutout.png`; venv reutilizable en `C:\Users\soporte\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\venv-rembg`
**Learned**:
- Pipeline ganador: generar con Gemini (fondo oscuro OK) → `rembg` local con modelo **`isnet-general-use`** + `alpha_matting=True` (fg=240, bg=10, erode=10) → PNG 32bppArgb con alfa real
- `u2net` (default de rembg) FALLA en escenas multi-objeto: deja solo la cabeza del robot o conserva blobs de fondo. ISNet conserva cuerpo completo + teléfono + iconos flotantes
- Instalación: `python -m venv` + `pip install rembg onnxruntime` (funciona en Python 3.14); modelos ~176MB se descargan en primer uso (quedan cacheados en `%USERPROFILE%\.u2net`)
- Verificación de alfa: System.Drawing → `PixelFormat` debe ser `Format32bppArgb` y esquinas A=0
- En componentes: quitar `mask-image` al usar cutouts (ya no es necesario); el glow radial detrás + float se mantienen
- Precios/effort: ISNet con alpha matting ~30s por imagen 1200x896 en CPU
